title: Output contract and fault-tolerance guidelines for tool-call flows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define a deterministic, testable acceptance surface for structured responses that invoke external tools/functions in streaming and non-streaming modes. This doc prioritizes developer ergonomics, safe degradation, and operational observability across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope: Acceptance criteria and edge-case behaviors for: schema anchoring, streaming fragments, resume tokens, tool-call invocation semantics (sync vs async), idempotency guarantees, error classification and automated fallbacks.

Non-goals: Full runtime implementation details; low-level kernel scheduling or batching heuristics (handled in ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canonical response envelope: Every response that may call tools MUST begin with an immutable header frame containing: schema_version, request_id, model_variant, sequence_origin, and a generated resume_token (opaque string).

2) Fragment framing and ordering: Streaming outputs MUST emit frames with monotonically increasing frame_index. The receiver can assemble final payload by concatenating validated frames in order. Frames that arrive out-of-order must be reordered using frame_index; missing frames are detected by gaps in sequence.

3) Resume semantics: resume_token + last_frame_index MUST be sufficient to request a resume from the service. A resume request returns frames starting from last_frame_index+1. Resume validity TTL = 10 minutes (configurable per deployment).

4) Schema anchoring and soft-validate mode: The header frame asserts a schema_id. The runtime must perform best-effort validation per-frame. If a frame fails validation, the runtime can emit a recoverable schema_warning frame and continue (soft-degrade). In strict mode (customer-configurable), the runtime must abort with a schema_error and a standard error code.

5) Tool call handshake: Tool-invoking frames must include tool_id, call_id, inputs (canonical JSON), and an expected idempotency_key. The service guarantees at-most-once execution for calls with idempotency_key when the underlying tool connector supports idempotency; otherwise the service will mark calls as best-effort and classify risk in telemetry.

6) Invocation modes: Synchronous tool calls (blocking) must return a tool_result frame before emitting subsequent content that depends on it. Asynchronous tool calls MAY emit a tool_pending frame and continue the stream; the tool_result frame must include call_id to allow correlation.

7) Error taxonomy and automatic fallbacks: Define three error classes: transient (retryable, maps to HTTP 503/429 analogs), degradable (tool failed but a graceful fallback exists, e.g., fallback_summary), and terminal (hard failure, abort stream). Acceptance requires explicit mapping of runtime errors to these classes and automated policy: transient -> up to 2 transparent retries; degradable -> emit fallback frame and continue; terminal -> emit terminal_error frame and close stream.

8) Partial-commit guarantees: When the model emits partial structured objects (e.g., incremental JSON objects), the runtime must provide a checkpoint frame at configurable intervals (default: every 4 frames or 1s) that marks a safe commit boundary for downstream consumers.

9) Observability and telemetry: Each session must emit structured events: session_start, frame_emitted, frame_validated, tool_call_initiated, tool_call_result, resume_requested, resume_success, resume_failure, session_end with latency and token counts. Error frames must include stable error_code and human_readable message.

10) Security and PII handling: Tool-call frames that include sensitive inputs MUST be tagged with pii_level and encrypt_at_rest=true metadata. Private deployment must enforce KMS-wrapped resume tokens when configured.

11) Backpressure and rate signals: If downstream cannot keep up, consumer may send a flow_control frame with desired_window; service must respect flow control within SLO bounds and emit a flow_paused frame if backpressure cannot be satisfied.

12) E2E testability: There must be automated e2e tests that simulate: normal streaming with synchronous tool calls, resume after mid-stream disconnect, schema deviation under soft-strict modes, transient tool failures and retry behavior, and backpressure-induced pauses. Acceptance criteria includes passing all tests in CI and sample load tests that demonstrate resume within TTL and no duplicate tool executions for idempotent keys.
out_of_scope:
- Implementation-level optimizations (kernel selection, batching internals)
- Authorization model for arbitrary tool connectors (covered in security tickets)
- Migration strategy for older APIs (handled separately)
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for header/frame generation and validation rules.
2) Integration tests: local mock tool connector verifies idempotency and result correlation across resume cycles.
3) Chaos tests: inject transient errors and verify retry and fallback policies.
4) Load tests: simulate 1k concurrent streaming sessions to validate telemetry volume and resume TTL behavior.
5) Compliance review: verify KMS-enforced resume tokens in Private deployment.

Acceptance: all tests green in the PR pipeline and a staged canary run (10% traffic) showing no regression in tail-latency or duplicate tool executions.
